title: Timeframes: same stock, different story
desc: Hourly, daily, weekly: zoom out before you decide

cards.title: Up or down?
cards.situation: The same stock, two charts. The hourly chart is falling. The daily chart is rising. Which one is right?

chart.label: Daily: three months rising from $80 to $100

options.feedback: The hourly chart only shows today’s small dip. Zoom out and the bigger move is up.

options.text: Up: longer charts are always right
options.feedback: Longer charts aren’t always right; they just cover more time. Both charts are true for their own time span.

options.text: Both: they show different time spans
options.feedback: Both are true. A small dip can sit inside a bigger rise.

cards.title: Pick your zoom
cards.text: Every chart has a **[[timeframe|timeframe]]**: how much time one candle covers. Same stock, same prices, different story.

blocks.tip: Short timeframes show noise. Long ones show the trend.

cards.title: Zoom out first
cards.text: Tap each timeframe, from the closest view out to the biggest. The same stock tells three different stories.

items.title: Daily · the pullback

chart.label: Daily candles pulling back from $58 to $52

items.line: …but it’s a bounce inside a pullback.

items.title: Weekly · the trend
items.line: And the pullback sits inside an uptrend. **Zoom out first.**

cards.title: Match the chart to your hold
cards.text: Holding for weeks? Trade from the **daily** chart. Holding for hours? The **hourly**. Always check one chart bigger first.

cards.title: Pick the chart
cards.q: You plan to hold a trade for 2 to 3 weeks. Which chart should you trade from?

options.feedback: 1-minute candles show noise you’ll never hold through. For weeks, use daily candles and check the weekly.
Hourly candles fit trades that last hours. For a hold of weeks, the daily chart shows the moves that matter.
Daily candles match a hold of weeks. Check the weekly chart first for the bigger trend.
Too zoomed out: your whole trade fits inside one monthly candle. Use the weekly for the big picture and trade from the daily.

cards.title: Big picture first
cards.q: The weekly chart is falling hard. The hourly chart shows a bounce. What should a beginner make of it?

options.text: Buy the bounce: it’s a new trend
options.feedback: A few hours up doesn’t turn a weekly downtrend. The bigger chart sets the trend.

options.text: Treat it as a bounce inside a downtrend
options.feedback: A few hours up inside a falling weekly chart is most likely a bounce. The bigger chart sets the trend.
The weekly chart is the big picture. Ignore it and you may buy a bounce in a downtrend.
Neither chart is wrong. They cover different time spans, and the longer one sets the trend.

cards.headline: You can zoom out before you decide.
lines: One candle can be a minute or a week.
Zoom out first: the bigger chart sets the trend.
Trade from the timeframe that matches your hold.
